Chapter 15. The Ongoing Journey—Praying Through Every Season
You know, parenting doesn’t really end just because your kids grow up. The seasons keep changing—there are graduations, weddings, new jobs, grandchildren, and sometimes, even losses. But no matter what, the heart of a parent? That stays the same.
Praying for adult children isn’t something you finish and check off a list. It’s an ongoing journey—always shifting, always teaching us something new. There’s challenge, for sure, but there’s also so much joy along the way.
I think about a couple who are now grandparents. They realized their prayers had changed over the years. Now, they ask for wisdom as their kids become parents themselves. They pray for patience as their children navigate the ups and downs of midlife, and for strength when loss comes. The way they pray might look different, but the love behind those prayers? That’s never changed.
Most people don’t really notice just how much the seasons of life shape the way we pray. Remember when you used to beg for your child’s safety? Over time, that turns into a prayer for legacy, for meaning, and for peace as the years go by. Parents keep learning how to adapt, and in the process, they discover that prayer isn’t just a ritual—it’s a lifelong conversation. It’s how we stay connected, how we find comfort and hope, no matter what life throws at us.
There’s this mother, facing her own health challenges, who found herself praying for her kids to find balance, to take care of themselves, to truly cherish family. She realized—her prayers were more than just words. They were a gift, a legacy, something she could pass down to the next generation.
The truth is, the journey’s never really finished. Through every season—whether it’s joy or sorrow, gain or loss, fresh starts or bittersweet endings—prayer stays with us. It’s the thread that weaves families together, the anchor that holds steady in every storm, and the light that guides us home.
